lesson_title: Motion Graphs: The Drawing That Does Your Physics
hook_text: Zero formulas. One sketch. Both accelerations AND 570 metres, read straight off it.
clip_script: Draw the bus trip as a velocity-time graph: a ramp climbing to 15 metres per second, a long plateau, a ramp easing back to zero. Now read it. Steepness is acceleration: the climb rises 15 in 6 — that is 2,5 metres per second squared. The plateau is level — zero. The fall sheds 15 across 10 — minus 1,5. And the area underneath is distance: a triangle, half of 6 times 15 — 45 metres. A rectangle, 30 times 15 — 450. A last triangle — 75. Total: 570 metres. Two accelerations and the whole distance, from one silhouette and primary-school geometry. That is why the velocity-time graph is the best bargain in Grade 10 physics.
visual_style: A flat-topped hill silhouette draws itself; slope values pop off each ramp, then the shape floods with colour as triangle-rectangle-triangle areas count up to 570.
pacing: Silhouette drawn fast, gradient reads snap in, area flood builds to the 570 reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and read a driver's feet straight off a graph.
